newsitem.title: USA: U.S. pilots say India's air control not a concern.
newsitem.headline: U.S. pilots say India's air control not a concern.

text.p: U.S. pilots flying into New Delhi, site of Tuesday's deadly mid-air crash, were not concerned about India's air traffic control system but did raise objections about health problems on the ground, a pilot's group said on Wednesday.
"The Indian air traffic control system is pretty by-the-book and professional," Kevin Dohm of the Airline Pilots Association in Chicago said.
"The only concern of United pilots was, to put it bluntly, the health problems on the ground. When laying over we had to make certain they had adequate hotels with sanitary conditions," he said.
Chicago-based United Airlines began daily flights into New Delhi last December as part of its around-the-world service that included stops in Los Angeles, Hong Kong, New Delhi and London.
The mid-air collision between a Saudi Arabia Airlines Boeing 747 and a Kazakh Ilyushin Il-76 freighter near New Delhi killed some 350 people.
